items: Combine them with `&&`, `||`, `!`
`$1 ~ /^a/` matches, `$1 !~ /^a/` does not match
A bare `/re/` always tests `$0`
awk keeps 'strnum' values, so comparison is type-aware
`$1 == 10` compares numerically IF field 1 looks numeric
Force it: `$1+0` for number, `$1""` for string
Uninitialized vars are both `""` and `0` at once
That is why `sum += $3` and `if (!seen[x])` need no setup
`if/else`, `while`, `do..while`, `for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)`, `for(k in arr)`
`break`, `continue`, `next` (skip to next record), `nextfile`
`exit` jumps straight to END
`print` adds ORS and joins with OFS; `printf` adds nothing
`sub(re,rep)` first match, `gsub(re,rep)` all matches
Both act on `$0` unless a third target is given
Both return the number of replacements made
`&` in the replacement means the match, `\\&` a literal ampersand

close(name)                # or run out of fds

blocks.title: Math & Escape Hatches
items: `int() sqrt() rand() srand()`, `%` modulo, `^` exponent
`system("cmd")` runs a shell command
`"cmd" | getline line` reads its output back
Keys are strings: `count["GET"]`, `count[$1]`, `count[1]` are one mechanism
`arr[k]++` auto-creates the element at 0, then increments
`k in arr` tests membership WITHOUT creating the key
`if (arr[k])` creates it — a classic long-running memory leak
`for (k in arr)` iterates in UNSPECIFIED order

blocks.title: When Order Matters
blocks.text: Pipe the loop output to `sort`, or set gawk's `PROCINFO["sorted_in"]="@val_num_desc"`.

items: `delete arr[k]` removes one key
`delete arr` clears the whole array (gawk / POSIX 2018)
`arr[a,b]` joins subscripts with `SUBSEP` (\034)
Split them back with `split(k, parts, SUBSEP)`

# group-and-sum: the report you write weekly
# NR==FNR is true only in the FIRST file

blocks.title: User Functions
items: `function f(a, b,   tmp) { ... }`
Params after the extra spaces are locals by convention
Every other variable in awk is global

blocks.title: Write POSIX, Reach Knowingly
blocks.text: Default to POSIX awk for portability; use gawk features on purpose, not by accident.

lines: # top talkers by IP, the whole shape in one line
| sort | uniq -c        # error rate by hour

items: Both inputs MUST be sorted the same way — no warning if not
Process substitution breaks the linear shape for two streams
`diff <(sort a) <(sort b)`, `comm -12 <(cut -f1 a|sort) ...`
Filter early, sort late — every dropped line is one sort never buffers
Collapse stages: `grep pat | awk '{print $2}'` is `awk '/pat/{print $2}'`
`cat f | grep x` is just `grep x f` (useless use of cat)
Debug by bisecting: append `| head -5`, or insert `| tee /tmp/s1 |`

lines: set -o pipefail   # any stage failing fails the pipe

blocks.title: Rule Of Thumb
blocks.text: Use the least powerful tool that solves it: smaller startup cost, faster runtime, and less to get wrong.

items: Speed per GB ASCII: cut/tr, then `grep -F`, grep ERE, mawk
Then sed, gawk, `grep -P`, then a Python script
End to end that span is often 10-50x
Memory: grep/sed/cut and array-free awk are O(1) in input
sort is O(n) and spills to disk; awk arrays are O(distinct keys)
`sort` and `awk END{}` block: nothing exits until input ends
So neither can sit mid-stream on a `tail -f`
Pipelines already use one core per stage
`sort --parallel`, `xargs -P`, `parallel --pipe` scale further
The cost of all three is reordered output

blocks.title: Free Speedups
items: `LC_ALL=C` kills UTF-8 collation and multibyte decode
Works for grep, sort and awk alike
Safe only when data is ASCII or byte order is acceptable
`grep -c` beats `grep | wc -l`: one less process and stream copy
POSIX grep/sed use a DFA: linear, no backtracking blowup
But no lookaround and no backreferences
PCRE buys power at the risk of blowup on `(a+)+b`
GNU-isms (`\b`, bare `sed -i`, `grep -P`, `sort -h`) die on BSD/busybox

blocks.title: Know When To Stop
blocks.text: Quoted-comma CSV, JSON, XML and multi-line records are NOT line-oriented. Reach for `jq`, `csvkit`, `xmlstarlet` or Python before writing unmaintainable sed.

blocks.title: Maintainability Wins
blocks.text: A readable 5-stage pipeline beats a clever awk one-liner nobody can modify — and a commented 15-line awk program beats both.

items: Double quotes let the shell eat `$`, backtick, `!` and `\` first
Single-quote every regex and every awk program
`grep 'foo(bar)'` hunts a LITERAL parenthesis
Symmetrically `grep -E 'a\+'` matches a literal plus

lines: grep -F '192.168.1.1' f  # or skip regex entirely

items: None of these errors — they just under-report
Always write `-k2,2` when you mean one field
Use awk's whitespace splitting instead of `cut -d' '`
`sed -i` with no backup on a bad regex destroys the file

blocks.title: Test Before -i
blocks.text: Run the sed without `-i` and eyeball it, or use `-i.bak`. There is no undo on a stream editor.

items: `&`, `\` and the delimiter must be escaped in a sed replacement
Unescaped, the substitution silently produces wrong text
CRLF makes `$` anchors and numeric compares fail invisibly
`grep 'foo$'` misses `foo\r` — fix with `tr -d '\r'` or dos2unix up front
`[a-z]` in a UTF-8 locale can match accented or upper chars
Use `[[:lower:]]` or `LC_ALL=C` for byte semantics
Filenames with spaces break `for f in $(grep -l ...)`
Use `-Z` with `xargs -0`, or `while IFS= read -r -d ''`

lines: # strnum bites hardest on zero-padded IDs

items: grep = select lines by pattern
Flags: `-i -v -w -o -c -n -r -E -F -P -q -A/-B/-C --include`
sed = per-line edit via read / execute / auto-print
Form: `[addr]s/re/rep/gpi`, plus `-n p`, `d`, `-i.bak`, `-E`, hold space

blocks.title: Escalation Path
blocks.text: Stop at the first tool on that ladder that does the job cleanly. Climbing further is a cost, not a win.

items: Single-quote patterns; escape your dots
Write `-k2,2`, never bare `-k2`
Sort before uniq; strip CRLF at the door
Set `LC_ALL=C` when you want byte semantics

blocks.title: Performance Checklist
items: Filter before sort, always
Prefer `-F` over a regex when the pattern is fixed
Merge adjacent grep+cut into one awk
Parallelize with `xargs -P` only AFTER measuring

blocks.title: Portability Checklist
items: Assume POSIX BRE/ERE only
Avoid `\b`, `\d`, `\K`, bare `sed -i`
Avoid `sort -h` and `grep -P` on macOS or busybox
0 / 1 / 2 from grep drives `if`, `&&`, and CI gates
`set -o pipefail` is what makes a multi-stage pipeline fail honestly
Without it you only ever see the LAST command's status

blocks.title: One Idea, Repeated
blocks.text: Text is lines, lines are fields, and small composable filters joined by pipes beat one large program.

caption.text: Part 2 of LINUX TEXT PROCESSING. Most people learn grep, sed and awk as three unrelated spells — and then spend years debugging the same four silent corruptions. This handbook teaches them as one system: lines, fields, and filters joined by pipes, with the BRE/ERE inversion, the sed cycle, awk's strnum rule, and why `sort -k2` almost never means what you think. 10 pages, no filler — the version I wish someone had handed me before my first 500 GB log.
